advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconcile the two Cloud credential guards (assert_env_ready vs _build_jira_backend) — extract a shared helper or delegate one to the other so whitespace/email rules and the message cannot drift.
evidence: backend.py:293-327 new guard uses `if not (value or "").strip()` plus an `@`/local/domain email check and a rich message
backend.py:194-202 assert_env_ready uses `if not value` (no strip), no email check, message 'missing JIRA_* configuration: ...'

_attestation.py:67-68 `backend = select_backend(load_config())` (constructs via _build_jira_backend → new guard) then `backend.assert_env_ready()` — the second check runs only if construction did not already raise, so its credential branch is dead in this path
The DC precedent placed the guard IN assert_env_ready (jira_datacenter/backend.py:353-386); Cloud instead added a parallel guard, leaving two sources of truth for the same invariant
advisory.finding: Cloud now has two divergent credential-presence guards: the new inline guard in _build_jira_backend (whitespace-strip + email-format) and the pre-existing JiraBackend.assert_env_ready (presence-only, no strip, no email check, different message). They can drift, and because select_backend() constructs the backend (triggering the new guard) before _attestation.py:68 calls assert_env_ready(), the assert_env_ready credential branch is effectively unreachable/dead for the attestation path.
scenarios: A future edit strengthens/weakens one guard but not the other, silently changing which callers reject whitespace-only or non-email JIRA_USER
A caller that invokes assert_env_ready() directly (not via the factory) still accepts a whitespace-only or non-email user that the factory rejects

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Align `JiraBackend.assert_env_ready()` with `_build_jira_backend`'s stricter credential validation (strip-based blank check + email-format check) so both fail-fast surfaces on the JIRA_URL/JIRA_USER/JIRA_API_TOKEN contract agree.
evidence: backend.py:194-202 `assert_env_ready`: `for name, value in (...JIRA_USER...) if not value` — no `.strip()`, no email-format check
backend.py:300 `_build_jira_backend`: `if not (value or "").strip()` plus backend.py:320-321 email check `local, sep, domain = s.user.strip().partition("@"); if not sep or not local or not domain:`

docs/adr/0035-reconciler-vendor-adapter-seam.md:187 documents `Backend.assert_env_ready()` as the fail-fast that 'checks JIRA_URL/JIRA_USER/JIRA_API_TOKEN'; it is called from src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/_attestation.py:68 for bootstrap-band execution
This is a within-module consistency drift on the credential-validation contract, not an external wire/CLI/config break — both surfaces still function and no external consumer distinguishes them
advisory.finding: The new construction-time credential guard in `_build_jira_backend` (strip-based blank detection + email-format check on JIRA_USER) is stricter than the sibling `JiraBackend.assert_env_ready()` fail-fast, which validates the SAME JIRA_URL/JIRA_USER/JIRA_API_TOKEN contract with only `if not value` (no strip, no email check). The two fail-fast surfaces on one credential contract now diverge (e.g. a whitespace-only or non-email JIRA_USER passes assert_env_ready but is rejected at construction).
advisory.suggested_fix: Extract the presence-strip-plus-email validation into a shared helper and call it from both `assert_env_ready()` and `_build_jira_backend`.
